title: Empirical verification of LLM-generated network configurations against deterministic network invariants
research_question: To what extent do LLM-generated network configurations produced from natural-language intents satisfy deterministic network invariants (reachability, policy compliance, loop-freedom) when evaluated by a deterministic verifier across realistic topologies and vendor-constraint templates?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: Single-shot LLM-generated configurations (baseline) will fail to satisfy a nontrivial fraction of deterministic network invariants across the sampled topology/task population.

H2: Applying an automated verifier-based guarded condition (generate→validate→repair with at most one repair call) will significantly reduce the fraction of invariant violations compared with single-shot baseline generation.
H3: Failures will concentrate on multi-device policy interactions and vendor-specific multi-device semantics rather than only per-device syntax errors.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: Which invariant types (reachability, ACL policy compliance, loop-freedom, route advertisement) dominate failures?
EQ2: How do pass/failure patterns vary by topology class (small, mid, multi-site) and vendor template family?
benchmark_scope: Public-device vendor configuration examples collected from vendor documentation and community repositories (explicit sources enumerated in evidence record list).
Synthetic realistic topologies generated deterministically per the adapter's challenging_workflow_stress_v1 index profile (very_hard and extreme task patterns only).
Isolated emulation using deterministic verifier (no live device execution).
model_scope: A single hosted-model provider per adapter contract (provider: openai_responses). Model metadata and generation settings are declared in the preregistration below and recorded for every call.
transformation_scope: baseline: direct_configuration_generation_v1 (one-shot generation from the intent + template)
guarded: generate_validate_repair_v1 (initial generation + deterministic verifier; if validator fails, one automatic repair-generation call allowed)
secondary_estimands: Per-invariant pass rates (paired difference guarded vs baseline) treated as exploratory
Failure-mode distribution proportions by topology and vendor family (exploratory descriptive)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design using the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Task_count fixed at 200 tasks. Episodes per task = 2 (baseline and guarded). Task indices selected deterministically with the adapter's challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile. Maximum_model_calls = task_count * 2 = 400. Selection and task indices are fixed before any hosted-model calls and not changed after observing outcomes. Inclusion: all generated tasks from the selected deterministic index list. Exclusion: a task is excluded only if the initial input intent or the provided vendor template is demonstrably malformed per deterministic syntactic pre-check (see transformation_validation). Excluded tasks will be reported; primary analysis treats excluded pairs according to the analysis executor failed_call_treatment policy (see analysis_plan).
analysis_plan: Confirmatory analysis executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed on per-task 'all-specified-invariants-pass' binary outcome. Primary hypothesis test: paired binary comparison (McNemar-style) implemented by the provided executor; report point estimate, 95% Wilson confidence interval for pass rates per condition, risk difference, and p-value. Primary failed-call handling: complete_pair_primary (complete the pair when both episodes available; see sensitivity analysis). Sensitivity analysis: treat any task with persistent unparsable outputs or excluded at generation time as failure for both conditions (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity) and report that result. All stratified subgroup analyses (topology class, vendor family, invariant-type) are explicitly labeled exploratory and not counted as additional confirmatory tests; no multiplicity adjustment is applied to exploratory analyses, but raw p-values and effect sizes are reported.
multiplicity_plan: Single predeclared primary estimand (paired success-rate difference). All other comparisons labeled exploratory. No confirmatory multiple-testing corrections beyond the single primary test.
missingness_plan: No human imputation. Deterministic preprocessing attempts to sanitize minor formatting issues (automatic sanitizer step described below). If a model output remains unparsable after the sanitizer and the guarded repair call (max one repair call allowed), the task is flagged as 'persistent unparsable'. Primary analysis: follow the executor's primary failed_call_treatment (complete_pair_primary). Sensitivity analysis: treat persistent unparsable tasks as failures for the affected condition(s) (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity). All excluded/persistent unparsable tasks and counts are logged and auditable.

risk_factors: poisoned or maliciously altered public example configs in community repositories
reuse of near-duplicate intent-template pairs leading to leakage
non-deterministic hosted-model behavior producing stochastic variability
detection_procedures: Deduplicate and checksum all vendor-template source files and record provenance (URL/DOI/record id) before use; detect duplicates by identical normalized token sequences.
Compute per-task divergence metrics (token-level similarity) between gold-source templates and generated configs; flag unusually high similarity as potential leakage.
Monitor per-task verifier outputs for systematic anomalies (e.g., identical failures across unrelated tasks) and log for automated post-hoc analysis.
item_flagging_rules: Flag any vendor-template source that is identical to a generated config (normalized whitespace/token-level match) and exclude that task from the confirmatory sample; the exclusion rule is deterministic and applied before model calls.

Flag tasks with persistent unparsable outputs after sanitizer+one repair call for sensitivity analysis; they remain in the primary analysis following failed_call_treatment rules but are listed as flagged.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged items are reported and analyzed separately; primary confirmatory analysis includes them per preregistered failed_call_treatment and sensitivity analysis treats persistent unparsables as failures.
residual_uncertainty: Residual risk that public vendor examples do not represent proprietary production templates (external-validity limitation).
Residual nondeterminism from the hosted-model provider when seeds are not supported.

budget_scenarios.description: Conservative reduced sample to validate pipeline and logs while minimizing model-call cost.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 100 tasks × up to 2 calls = 200 maximum model calls, within the manifest model-call budget; useful smoke-test of pipeline and artifact retention.

budget_scenarios.description: Predeclared primary confirmatory plan as preregistered: 200 tasks sampled from the adapter's deterministic stress profile.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 200 tasks produce up to 400 model calls (1 initial generation + at most 1 repair per task). 400 ≤ 10,000 model-call manifest limit and is executable within the seven-day wall-clock bound using hosted APIs with parallel orchestration and deterministic logging.

budget_scenarios.description: Extended exploratory sample to increase precision and permit finer subgroup estimates.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 400 tasks × up to 2 calls = 800 calls; still ≤ manifest budget but increases runtime and artifact volume. Recommended only if additional compute budget and time are available.

power_plan.target_effect: Detect an absolute increase in 'all-invariants-pass' rate of 10–15 percentage points (guarded vs baseline) with 80% power at α=0.05 (two-sided) as a planning target.
power_plan.clustering_unit: task (paired: baseline vs guarded per task)
power_plan.calculation_method: Paired-binary (McNemar-approximation) planning. Because prior baseline pass-rate is uncertain, planning uses sensitivity bands: if baseline pass rate ≈ 50–60%, N=200 provides ~80% power to detect an absolute paired difference of ~12–15 percentage points under reasonable paired discordance assumptions. Exact power will be reported post-run using observed discordant cell counts and the executor's paired test implementation.
assumptions: Baseline pass-rate assumed between 0.45 and 0.65 for planning.
Discordant-pair proportions consistent with moderate effect sizes in prior code/validator literature.
Maximum one repair call per task (adapter constraint) and deterministic verification outcomes.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=200 tasks, the minimum detectable absolute paired difference at 80% power depends on observed discordance; planning aims at detecting ≈12–15 percentage points under mid-range baseline assumptions. Sensitivity analyses will report the exact detectable effect given observed data.
sensitivity_analyses: Report power post-hoc given observed baseline pass rate and discordant counts.
Sensitivity using conservative treatment of persistent unparsable tasks as failures (alternative failed-call treatment).

semantic_equivalence_checks: Deterministic parser will extract intent-key items (interfaces, prefixes, ACL names) from generated configs and confirm presence/consistency with the input intent using rule-based checks.

Verifier invariants (reachability, ACL compliance, loop-freedom, route advertisement constraints) are used as semantic checks: a configuration that fails any declared invariant is semantically incorrect for this study's operational goal.
automatic_rejection_rules: If a generated configuration fails deterministic parsing after the automatic_syntax_sanitizer_v1 step and the permitted guarded repair call does not produce a parseable config, mark the generation as 'persistent unparsable' and follow preregistered failed-call treatment (no manual intervention).
If a generated configuration is identical (token-normalized match) to a vendor source template that would cause leakage, exclude the task deterministically prior to model calls.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deterministic audit sample: 10% of tasks selected by seeded RNG (seed recorded) undergo full byte-level artifact snapshot comparisons and additional verifier assertion re-runs to ensure deterministic scoring. All verification logs and artifacts are retained.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: All template-to-config mappings and parser rules (token normalization, canonicalization, ACL canonical ordering) are implemented deterministically in code and versioned; their unit tests and outputs are retained as reproducibility evidence.
residual_risks: Deterministic parser coverage may miss vendor-specific idiosyncrasies not present in public templates.
Hosted-model nondeterminism if provider does not support seeds; temperature set to 0.0 but true determinism not guaranteed.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Representativeness of public vendor templates compared with proprietary production device templates (external validity).
Hosted-model provider nondeterminism when service-level seeding is unsupported (mitigated but not eliminated by temperature=0.0).
Task population limited to adapter's challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile (very_hard/extreme); results do not claim generalization to all NetOps tasks.
